== Biography ==
John B. Glasgow Jr. was born on 15 April 1814 in County Tyrone, Ireland. He was the fourth of seven children of [[Glasgow-1968|John Glasgow]] and [[Unknown-764117|Jane]].<ref name="HillsdaleJohn">''Portrait and Biographical Album of Hillsdale County, Michigan'' (Chicago: Chapman Brothers, 1888), [https://archive.org/details/portraitbiograph00chpm/page/688/mode/1up p. 688]; [https://www.migenweb.org/hillsdale/bios/bios-g.html transcription].</ref><ref name="HillsdaleWilliam">''Portrait and Biographical Album of Hillsdale County, Michigan'' (Chicago: Chapman Brothers, 1888), [https://archive.org/details/portraitbiograph00chpm/page/395/mode/1up p. 395]; [https://www.migenweb.org/hillsdale/bios/bios-g.html transcription].</ref>

An older brother emigrated to the United States in 1833. John followed in 1839 and first joined him at Auburn, New York. In August 1843 John moved to Fayette Township, Hillsdale County, Michigan, where he farmed on section 7.<ref name="HillsdaleJohn" />

John married three times. His first wife was [[Eddy-4623|Elizabeth "Betsey" Eddy]], widow of a Mr. Hoagland. Only one child of that marriage survived to adulthood: Mary J. Glasgow, later wife of James Gould of Wheeling, Missouri.<ref name="HillsdaleJohn" />

His second wife was [[Sinclair-10598|Mary J. Sinclair]], who died about 1872. Their two named children were Walter Glasgow, husband of Dora Miller and resident of Fayette Township, and Rose B. Glasgow, wife of Cassius Clark of Allen Township.<ref name="HillsdaleJohn" />

John's third wife was [[Babbitt-880|Mary Ann Babbitt]], widow of Laban Howard. They married on 19 January 1876 at Allen, Hillsdale County.<ref name="HillsdaleJohn" />

John died on 22 April 1893 in Hillsdale County, Michigan.<ref>{{FindAGrave|42540370}}</ref>

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-1968]] is assessed at 98% (proved). The 1888 Hillsdale biographies pp 688 and 395 identify John B., born 15 April 1814, as one of John and Jane’s seven children. Named siblings and the Auburn-to-Hillsdale sequence define John-1968 despite contradictory parental birthplaces and 1844/1848 migration dates.

Whole selected father-profile proposition; maternity and upstream ancestry assessed separately.

Next useful test: Compare the 1888 sketches with a contemporary family or probate record.

Source basis already held: [https://archive.org/details/portraitbiograph00chpm/page/688/mode/1up Portrait and Biographical Album of Hillsdale County, Michigan (Chicago: Chapman Brothers, 1888), p. 688 (https://archive.org/details/portraitbiograph00chpm/page/688/mode/1up); transcription (https://www.migenweb.org/hillsdale/bios/bios-g.html).]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.



The 1888 biography of John says his parents were born in Scotland and moved to County Tyrone after marriage. William's biography in the same volume says they were born in County Tyrone to Scottish parents. Both accounts agree on this sibling group and its later migration.

No compatible WikiTree profiles have yet been established for John's children Mary J., Walter or Rose B. Same-name profiles should not be attached without records connecting them to Hillsdale County and the named spouses.

The 1879 county history also discusses the Glasgow family on page 263.<ref>''History of Hillsdale County, Michigan'' (Philadelphia: Everts & Abbott, 1879), [https://archive.org/details/bad0928.0001.001.umich.edu/page/263/mode/1up p. 263].</ref>
